messages:
tina: FYI canary run #2 with mix-precision flagged a latency spike and a few malformed invoice fields in structured output. p95 ~ +12% and field-drop ~+0.9%.

sam: do we have the CI link + profiler logs?

tina: https://ci.internal/runs/2039876543 - profiler attached. quick paste below.

maya: looking at profiler: a lot of kernel churn around mid-stack; when seq > 1024 we see fallback to int8_generic for a few layers and a kv miss spike.

```text
[10:21:12] layer8 sel_kernel=fp8_fast_v2
[10:21:12] layer9 sel_kernel=int8_generic
[10:21:12] layer10 sel_kernel=int8_generic
[10:21:12] layer11 sel_kernel=fp8_fast_v2
[10:21:12] kernel_switches=7
[10:21:12] kv_cache_hit_rate=0.87 kv_miss_spike seq=1025
```

alex: that seq=1025 boundary jumps out. we recently bumped batching pad align to 64; that could change effective seq distribution and kernel selection paths.

sam: can we repro with the exact batcher flags? run eval harness with trace-kernel and seed.

tina: started local repro: ./tools/run_eval.py --model bert-invoice --profile --mixprec=auto --kv=true --batch-pad=64 --seq-len=1100

ci-bot: ci job started run_id=ci-2039876543-2

maya: calibration note: layer9 scale differs slightly (0.0023 vs expected 0.0025) after online calib. small scale shift moves activations across quant buckets and can flip token choices in our greedy structured postproc.

alex: so likely two factors: (1) kernel selection churn incurring memcpy/re-quant cost, (2) tiny calibration drift for certain layers causing structured decode flips. both could be triggered by padding/alignment change.

sam: plan: A/B tests - A keep adaptive switching (kernel_policy=prefer_fp8) with online calib; B force fp8-only and use static calib table. also run with kv disabled to isolate.

tina: launching A/B:
- A: kernel_policy=prefer_fp8 mixprec=auto calib=online
- B: kernel_policy=force_fp8 mixprec=fp8-only calib=static

maya: baseline deltas: BLEU -0.6, EM -1.2, structured-drop +0.9%.

alex: results: A p95 still +9% structured-drop +0.8% (bad). B p95 back to baseline and structured-drop -0.1% (good). kv-disabled: quality fine but latency worsens.

maya: conclusion: calibration + kernel selection churn caused quality regression; KV affects latency but not the structured corruption.

alex: actions:
- eng-runtime: revert pad alignment to 32 and add unit test around seq=1024 (owner alex)
- eng-ml: produce static per-layer calibration for bert-invoice and publish in model bundle (owner maya)
- devex: add CI eval that runs invoice structured set under mixprec policies (owner sam)
- ops: roll kernel_policy=prefer_fp8 to 10% for a day as a quick mitigation (owner tina)

tina: drafted rollout and linked the batcher change commit https://repo/internal/commit/abc123

sam: also add a microbenchmark for kernel-switch cost at seq=[900,1024,1100,2048]; if switch cost >3ms we avoid mid-batch switching.

ci-bot: ci job finished artifacts at https://ci.internal/artifacts/2039876543

maya: opening PR eng-ml/static-calib-invoice with table + test.

alex: opening PR to revert pad and add seq boundary test.

tina: update 2039876599 - canary at 10% with kernel_policy=prefer_fp8 for 2h, no regressions observed. scheduling pad rollback next week, will update thread when done.

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
